correctness.rationale: The canonical fixed-support formula \(w(A)=mn+|A|-q(A)\) is exact. The direct two-support census covers same-row, same-column, and distinct-row-column cases, each with strictly positive excess. With \(|A|\ge3\), the row/column counts prove both inequalities in RESULT.md, forcing equality only when \(m=n=3\) and \(|A|=3\); then every row and column must contain precisely one selected cell. There are six such supports, alongside the \(mn\) one-cell supports. The executable checks independently reconstruct adjacency and verify 1,188,352 complete small-board support cases and 551,124 full ternary labelings. Computational tests are finite corroboration, not the infinite proof.

Detailed comparisons of exact statements and the classification of all minimizers did not find coverage. residual_risks: Unindexed earlier work might phrase the theorem as perfect Roman domination of complements of rectangular rook graphs or unique-neighbor grid guard functions.

value.rationale: The classification settles a natural graph invariant on every two-factor direct product of complete graphs, not merely individual orders. It gives all optimal functions and a sharp exceptional permutation configuration at \(K_3\times K_3\). Compared with the established ordinary Roman number \(6\) when both factors have order at least four, the perfect number \(m+n\) yields an unbounded additive separation, a structurally motivated effect of the unique-defender constraint.
